questiontext.text: In the MBT Workflow, what does the Model stage do?

answer.text: Turns the informal spec into a precise behavioral model, typically a finite-state machine

feedback.text: Correct — the Model stage captures the states the system can be in and the events that move it between them.

answer.text: Runs the concrete tests against the real system

feedback.text: That is the Execution stage, not Model.

answer.text: Maps abstract events onto real API calls and data values

feedback.text: That is Concretization, not Model.

answer.text: Compares observed behavior against predicted behavior

feedback.text: That is the Conformance verdict, not Model.

generalfeedback.text: The Model stage turns an informal spec into a precise behavioral model (typically an FSM). Everything downstream is derived from it, so a wrong model means wrong tests.

name.text: What the Generation criterion stage does

questiontext.text: What is the job of the Generation criterion stage?

answer.text: Choose how thoroughly to exercise the model, turning it into a set of test obligations

feedback.text: Correct — the criterion decides whether to cover every state, transition, transition-pair, or round-trip path.

answer.text: Pick real input values for each event

feedback.text: That happens during Concretization, not when choosing the criterion.

answer.text: Record the outputs observed at each step

feedback.text: That is Execution, not the Generation criterion.

answer.text: Rewrite the informal spec into an FSM

feedback.text: That is the Model stage; the criterion comes after the model exists.

generalfeedback.text: The Generation criterion chooses how thoroughly the model is exercised (every state, every transition, every adjacent pair, or every round-trip path) and turns the model into a concrete set of test obligations.

name.text: What "abstract" means in the abstract test suite

questiontext.text: Why are the tests in the Abstract test suite called "abstract"?

answer.text: They are model-level event sequences that name events, not real API calls or data values yet

feedback.text: Correct — an abstract test is a sequence like "validCard · push · timeout" with no concrete values.

answer.text: They describe the architecture rather than the behavior

feedback.text: Abstract here means model-level events, not architecture.

answer.text: They have already been run against the real system

feedback.text: Running happens later, in Execution; abstract tests have no real values yet.

answer.text: They contain concrete API calls but no expected outputs

feedback.text: Abstract tests contain no concrete API calls at all; those are added during Concretization.

generalfeedback.text: Abstract tests are event sequences at the model level (e.g. "validCard · push · timeout"). They name events, not real API calls or data values — those are supplied during Concretization.

questiontext.text: What does the Concretization stage do?

answer.text: Maps each abstract event onto a concrete action against the real system and picks real input values

feedback.text: Correct — this is where the model meets the actual system under test (SUT).

answer.text: Chooses which coverage criterion to satisfy

feedback.text: That is the Generation criterion, not Concretization.

answer.text: Judges whether the system conformed to the model

feedback.text: That is the Conformance verdict, not Concretization.

answer.text: Builds the finite-state machine from the spec

feedback.text: That is the Model stage.

generalfeedback.text: Concretization maps each abstract event onto a concrete action (an API call, a UI gesture, a clock advance) and picks real input values. It is where the model meets the actual SUT.

questiontext.text: What does the Execution stage do?

answer.text: Runs the concrete test against the SUT and records the observed outputs and state transitions

feedback.text: Correct — Execution records what actually happens at each step.

answer.text: Derives abstract event sequences from the model

feedback.text: That is the Abstract test suite stage, not Execution.

answer.text: Selects real input values for each abstract event

feedback.text: That is Concretization, which precedes Execution.

answer.text: Decides whether the model omits an important state

feedback.text: That concern belongs to the Model stage.

generalfeedback.text: Execution runs the concrete test against the SUT and records what actually happens at each step: the observed outputs and state transitions.

questiontext.text: What does the Conformance verdict stage do?

answer.text: Compares the observed SUT behavior against what the model predicted

feedback.text: Correct — match means pass; divergence means fail, and the failing step localizes the problem.

answer.text: Chooses how thoroughly to exercise the model

feedback.text: That is the Generation criterion.

answer.text: Turns the informal spec into a behavioral model

feedback.text: That is the Model stage.

answer.text: Maps abstract events onto real API calls

feedback.text: That is Concretization.

generalfeedback.text: The Conformance verdict compares observed SUT behavior against what the model predicted. A match yields pass; a divergence yields fail, and the failing step pinpoints either a system bug or a model that no longer matches reality.

questiontext.text: Abstract test 2 is just invalidCard. Which transition does it exercise, and what is special about it?

answer.text: Locked → Locked — a self-loop, since an invalid card leaves the door locked

feedback.text: Correct — invalidCard is the self-loop that keeps the door Locked.

answer.text: Locked → Unlocked — it unlocks the door

feedback.text: Only a valid card unlocks; invalidCard leaves the door locked.

answer.text: Open → Locked — it re-locks the door

feedback.text: That is the timeout transition, not invalidCard.

answer.text: Unlocked → Open — it opens the door

feedback.text: That is the push transition.

generalfeedback.text: invalidCard exercises the self-loop Locked --invalidCard--> Locked: the door stays locked on an invalid card.

questiontext.text: The spec is changed so the door re-locks after 10 s instead of 5 s, but the FSM's timeout is left at 5 s. Which failure mode is this, and what do the tests then verify?

answer.text: Model drift — the tests verify yesterday's 5 s behavior, not the current 10 s spec

feedback.text: Correct — an un-updated model makes tests check stale behavior.

answer.text: Bad input data — the wrong concrete value was chosen

feedback.text: Here the model itself is stale; it is not a concretization value problem.

answer.text: Observability gap — the timeout cannot be observed

feedback.text: The timeout is observable; the issue is that the model was not updated.

answer.text: Infeasible sequence — the timeout order is unreachable

feedback.text: The sequence is still feasible; the model is simply out of date.

generalfeedback.text: Model drift: the spec changes but the model is not updated, so the tests verify yesterday's behavior (the old 5 s timeout) rather than the current spec.

name.text: Why abstract tests must be concretized before execution

questiontext.text: Execution runs against the real SUT, yet the abstract test validCard · push · timeout cannot be run directly. Why must concretization happen first?

answer.text: Abstract tests only name events with no real API calls or values; concretization supplies the concrete actions and values needed to run

feedback.text: Correct — the SUT needs real calls and values, which concretization provides.

answer.text: The verdict must be computed before execution can start

feedback.text: The verdict is the last stage; it cannot precede execution.

answer.text: The generation criterion is re-chosen at execution time

feedback.text: The criterion is fixed much earlier; it is not re-chosen at execution.

answer.text: The model is rebuilt from the observed outputs first

feedback.text: Execution does not rebuild the model; it runs the concretized test.

generalfeedback.text: Abstract tests are model-level event sequences with no real API calls or data values. Concretization maps each event onto a concrete action (e.g. reader.swipe(card="EMP-4417")) and real values, which is what Execution needs to run against the SUT.
